introduction_markdown: Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board, General Certificate of Education Examination, June 2020, Ordinary Level, Physics, Paper 2 (subject code 0580). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section II in 1 1/2 hours. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section II answer EITHER the a, b and c OR the d, e and f of each question. For your guidance the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Calculators are allowed.

Figure 2 shows a bar magnet, N-S, held near a coil wound around a cardboard tube, and which is connected to a galvanometer, G.

figures.legende: Figure 2: bar magnet S-N placed to the left of a coil wound round a cardboard tube, connected in series with a galvanometer G.

incertitudes: Question 3 (c) : le sujet ne précise pas le sens de l'enroulement ; la réponse retenue est fondée sur la loi de Lenz (pôle nord induit côté aimant), sans dessiner les spires.

questions.enonce_markdown: Copy the diagram and draw the magnetic flux pattern for the bar magnet. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Copy the magnet, the coil and the galvanometer. Around the magnet draw several smooth **closed field lines** that **leave the N pole, curve round outside the magnet and enter the S pole**, with arrows on the lines pointing away from N and towards S. The lines are closest together near the poles (where the field is strongest), they never cross, and they are spread further apart away from the magnet. *(The drawing is made by the candidate.)*

questions.enonce_markdown: State what will be observed on the galvanometer if the magnet is moved rapidly towards the coil. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: The galvanometer pointer **deflects** (briefly, to one side of zero) because an e.m.f. and a current are induced in the coil while the magnet is moving; it returns to zero when the magnet stops moving.

questions.enonce_markdown: Draw the magnetic flux pattern for the coil as the magnet approaches it. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: By Lenz's law the induced current flows in the direction that opposes the approach of the N pole of the magnet. The end of the coil **facing the magnet becomes a north pole**, and the far end becomes a south pole. The coil then behaves like a short bar magnet: draw closed field lines that **leave the end of the coil facing the magnet (N), loop round outside the coil and enter the other end (S)**, and pass through the inside of the coil from the S end to the N end, with arrows showing this direction. *(The drawing is made by the candidate.)*
